clue.text: Press testament of inflexible determination

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
a last will and testament is a will

explanation.surface: Someone's pressing evidence shows how stubborn they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbending resolve is described as having a will made of metal, an idiom for steely firmness.

clue.text: Scaler of rocks in the fresh air

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber of crags is out in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like what the climber scales, but it is the anagram signal working on the eight letters of SCALER OF.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian borrowing describes doing something outdoors, such as dining outside.

clue.text: Colonel's unit cut down course of exercise

indicators.note: cut down tells us to chop the bottom, the final letter, off the word for the unit

parts.note: a colonel commands a regiment

explanation.surface: A colonel's troops are reduced to a training programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' removes the T at the end of REGIMENT; in a down clue the last letter is the bottom one.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed plan of diet or exercise followed for health.

clue.text: Sprinkles sprigs of flowers

definitions.meaning: to sprinkle is to scatter drops over something, a verb in the third person
small branches or bunches of blossom

explanation.surface: Someone scatters water over little bunches of blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both scatters liquid in drops and small decorative bunches of blossom, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Ringleader plunged into battle: what a horrid sight

indicators.note: plunged into says one piece is thrust inside the other

parts.note: a battle is a fight
the leader of Ring is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A gang boss charges into the fray, a ghastly spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringleader' reads as a gang boss, but it gives the first letter of 'Ring', which 'plunged into' puts inside FIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a grotesque or ridiculous-looking person or thing is called a fright, as in 'she looked a fright'.

clue.text: Apoplectic ruler with the flutters

parts.note: someone apoplectic with rage goes purple in the face
an emperor is a ruler

explanation.surface: A furious monarch is seized with nervous palpitations.
explanation.walkthrough: The purple emperor is a large British butterfly; 'with the flutters' points to a creature that flutters, not a nervous ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly is a fluttering insect, and this is the name of one species.

clue.text: A real idiot. Correct the nephew of a fabulous aunt

parts.note: correct means proper

parts.words: the nephew of a fabulous aunt
parts.note: Charley's Aunt is a famous Victorian stage farce; Charley is the nephew whose aunt is impersonated

explanation.surface: A complete fool is put right about a famous comic aunt's nephew.
explanation.walkthrough: Charley's Aunt (1892) is a long-running British farce. 'Proper charley' is British slang for an utter fool.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a charley is a fool, and proper intensifies it to mean a complete one.

clue.text: Unwise assertion that the conditions were measly?

definitions.meaning: a hasty, ill-considered claim or remark
a declaration that the state of things was spotty, like measles

explanation.surface: Someone makes a careless claim that things were pretty poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measly' means paltry, but literally it means having measles, whose symptom is a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasty, careless declaration is called rash, and the second reading takes rash as the skin spots of measles.

clue.text: His work should be in mint condition

definitions.text: His work should be in mint condition

parts.words: His work should be in mint condition
parts.note: mint condition usually means pristine, but read literally it is the state of coins freshly struck at a mint, whose maker is described

explanation.surface: A craftsman's output ought to be immaculate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strikes coins produces money, as at the Mint, or forges it.

clue.text: When one Bank Holiday is not impressive?

parts.note: the prefix in- means not, as in inactive
august means grand or impressive

explanation.surface: Asking when a public holiday falls, or calling it unimpressive.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain there is a Bank Holiday (a public holiday) at the end of the eighth month of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bank Holiday in Britain falls on the last Monday of that summer month, so this phrase says when it happens.

clue.text: Sort of wood pelmet, but lacking fit

indicators.note: lacking says the letters for the fit are missing from the word for the curtain box

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'

explanation.surface: A carpenter's pelmet made of some timber doesn't fit.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P, E and T out of PELMET, in that order, and three letters remain. A pelmet is a box hiding curtain fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tree whose timber is used as a hardwood.

clue.text: About the failure to reach target-it's altogether negligent

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a miss is a shot that fails to hit

explanation.surface: Missing the target is considered thoroughly careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careless in carrying out one's duty is a synonym, as in remiss of you.

clue.text: No difficulty getting labour for this!

definitions.text: No difficulty getting labour for this!

parts.words: No difficulty getting labour for this!
parts.note: a piece of work that needs no struggle; labour here is the job itself, not workers to hire

explanation.surface: An employer has no trouble finding workers for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple job, one requiring little effort, is the meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: Scold to pay up.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for pay is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone is nagged into settling a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pay up' looks like a demand, but 'up' turns PAY backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag or chatter shrilly at someone is a sense of this word, as a small dog yelps.

clue.text: Cut some curved edges on a slice of veal

definitions.meaning: to trim an edge into a series of semicircles, a verb
a thin boneless cut of meat, an escalope

explanation.surface: A cook trims the wavy rim of a piece of veal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both shaping an edge in a row of curves like a shell's rim and a thin escalope of meat.

clue.text: Throw up a pill?

definitions.meaning: to toss something high into the air
pill is old slang for a ball, and a high slow ball can be named by this word

explanation.surface: Being sick after swallowing a tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' looks like vomiting and 'pill' a tablet; in sports slang a pill is a ball, and a high ball is so called in tennis or cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both hurling something in a high arc and a ball sent up high, pill being slang for a ball.

clue.text: Puts the lid on Brown for getting wind of a cable

definitions.text: for getting wind of a cable

parts.note: to cap something is to put a lid on it
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: Someone seals a brown container to learn of a telegram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting wind of' looks like hearing news, but it means winding: the machine winds a ship's rope or anchor cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship around which rope or chain is wound.

clue.text: A Crimean development from The States

indicators.note: a development is a change of form, so these letters are reshaped into another order

explanation.surface: An event in the Crimea that originates in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' is the anagram signal working on the letters of A CRIMEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something originating in the United States is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Keep a supply of drugs the soup-kitchen?

parts.note: to stock goods is to keep a supply of them
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiles narcotics at a charity kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup-kitchen' suggests a charity for the hungry; here it is taken literally as the pan where stock and soup are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pan in which stock for soups is simmered is a kitchen vessel for making soup.

clue.text: Agitated man seizing Benn with a word to the contrary

indicators.note: seizing says the shuffled word grabs and holds the other piece inside it
agitated means stirred up, so the letters of man are shaken into a new order

parts.note: Tony Benn was a well-known British Labour politician

explanation.surface: An excited man grabs a Labour politician with a dissenting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' makes ANM from MAN, and 'seizing' puts TONY between AN and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A word opposite in meaning to another, such as hot to cold, is what this term means.

clue.text: Jane broke a horse in for a period after Elizabeth

indicators.note: in says the horse is placed inside the jumbled letters
broke means smashed apart, so the letters of the name and the article are reassembled

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy, short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A woman tames a horse during the Elizabethan aftermath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like breaking in a horse, but it jumbles JANE plus A, and 'in' puts COB inside. The reign of James I followed Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the reign of James I of England, which followed the Elizabethan age.

clue.text: The criminal clearly isn't a relative by marriage

definitions.meaning: a fugitive lawbreaker beyond legal protection

definitions.text: clearly isn't a relative by marriage
definitions.meaning: a relative by marriage is an in-law

explanation.surface: A crook is plainly not one of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: In-laws are relatives by marriage, so the opposite of 'in' gives the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive who has broken the law is the plain meaning, and the second sense plays on in-law versus out-law.

clue.text: Shutter usually closed at night

parts.note: a shutter sounds like a window cover, but here it is the fold of skin that covers the eye during sleep

explanation.surface: A window shutter that is normally shut after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin fold closing over the eye shuts out light, and it is generally shut while we sleep.

clue.text: Struck a match on the run

definitions.text: Struck a match on the run

parts.words: Struck a match on the run
parts.note: striking a match suggests lighting one while running, but here a match is a marriage, made by a couple who run off

explanation.surface: Someone lit a match while running.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who run away secretly to marry make a match while fleeing.

clue.text: It can make road repairs. work of art

indicators.note: work of tells us the letters of art are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Fixing a road counts as a work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work of art' reads as a masterpiece, but 'work of' is the anagram signal applied to ART.
explanation.definitionFit: This black substance is used to surface and patch roads.

clue.text: On the move Halle got very fashionable

indicators.note: on the move means shifting about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: On tour, the Halle orchestra became the height of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Halle is a Manchester orchestra. 'On the move' is the anagram signal for HALLE and GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British phrase for something greatly in vogue or popular.

clue.text: Moor wild, likely

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of likely are scrambled

explanation.surface: A moor is probably wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' is not a verb or a person: Ilkley Moor is a Yorkshire moorland, famous from the song 'On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: This West Yorkshire town gives its name to a well-known stretch of upland heath.

clue.text: Jan. 1 to Dec. 31; a long, long time

definitions.meaning: taken literally, from the first day of a calendar year to its last

explanation.surface: From New Year's Day to New Year's Eve, an age.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means constantly over a long period, and literally spans from the start to the end of a twelve-month.
